title: Medicare Levy Amendment (Attribution Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015
short_title: Medicare Levy Amendment (Attribution Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would extend Medicare levy provisions to certain tax liabilities of attribution managed investment trust trustees under the proposed new trust taxation system.
It would include the levy when trustees are taxed on income allocation shortfalls, complementing the income tax rates specified by a companion bill.
These amendments would operate with the broader managed investment trust reform package and apply to specified trustee liabilities arising under its income allocation rules.
changes: The levy would apply when a member’s attributed assessable income is less than the amount that should have been attributed.
The levy would apply when total assessable income allocated to members falls below the relevant trust component.
The levy would apply to shortfalls arising when previously understated assessable income is not properly carried forward.
summary.affected: Trustees of attribution managed investment trusts with the specified income shortfalls would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Alex Hawke
speeches.brief: The Medicare Levy Amendment (Attribution Managed Investment Trusts) Bill 2015 amends the Medicare Levy Act 1986 to impose the two per cent Medicare levy on trustees of attribution managed investment trusts when they do not attribute all income to members, ensuring that income does not escape taxation.

speeches.speaker: Kelly O'Dwyer
speeches.brief: The bills create a new tax system for eligible managed investment trusts, reducing compliance costs by $30 million per year and taxing investors directly, modernising rules for Australia’s $2.6 trillion funds management industry.

speeches.speaker: Angus Taylor
speeches.brief: A motion was moved requesting the Senate to resume consideration of 14 specified bills from the previous session, with each request to be conveyed in a separate message. The bills covered water amendment, managed investment trusts, social services, crime commission, deaths registration, tax and superannuation, crowd-sourced funding, firearms trafficking, and parliamentary entitlements.
